claim_type_rationale: Single-master Wikipedia 'Research stations in Antarctica' article supplies the universe scope (master's 'Permanent active stations' table inclusion-as-permanent-active row) + value cells for all 4 staged columns. Master's 4-partition structure (Permanent active stations table / Subantarctic stations subsection / Summer-only active stations table / Inactive stations table) defines the universe via the boolean conjunction filter (active=true AND operating_schedule=year-round AND source_partition='Permanent active stations table') which selects the 43-row Permanent-active partition. The in-scope partition includes Antarctic island stations (King George Island, Laurie Island, Anvers Island, Adelaide Island, Ross Island, Marambio Island, Galindez Island, etc.) alongside continental-interior stations; the article's separate 'Subantarctic stations' subsection (9 rows: Macquarie / Crozet / South Georgia / Kerguelen / Marion etc.) is the master-defined boundary for what counts as 'Antarctic' vs 'Subantarctic'. SQL-WHERE = `status = 'active' AND operating_schedule = 'year-round' AND source_partition = 'permanent_active_stations_table'`. The deterministic-universe-rule preference is satisfied — the source's 4-partition structure makes the boolean filter operation source-visible (no curator-judgment beyond the scope-restriction to the master-defined Permanent-active partition).

PIVOT context: 5th-of-13-floor-lift candidate this session after multiple set_filter source-friction attempts (canals duplicate; lighthouses fragmented; IGOs fragmented; UNESCO Danger List 403; glaciers fragmented; volcanic-eruptions VEI≥5 set-filter-vs-comparative ambiguity). Antarctic research stations has the cleanest set_filter shape because Wikipedia's master article literally provides 4 separate partition tables, so the boolean filter operation is source-visible.

excluded_from_universe.subantarctic_stations_subsection: 9 rows in master's 'Subantarctic stations' subsection — out of scope because master article explicitly partitions Subantarctic stations away from Antarctic stations. Master-listed Subantarctic stations are on islands north of the Antarctic Convergence (Macquarie / Crozet / South Georgia / Kerguelen / Marion Island etc.) and the master treats them as a distinct partition from the Antarctic 'Permanent active stations' table. Cycle-2 audit fix: earlier prose described the in-scope partition as 'continental-only' which was factually wrong — many in-scope rows ARE on Antarctic islands (King George Island ×9, Laurie Island, Anvers Island, Adelaide Island, Ross Island ×2, etc.). The correct boundary is the master's Antarctic-vs-Subantarctic partition, NOT a continental-vs-island distinction.

excluded_from_universe.inactive_stations_table: 69 rows in master's 'Inactive stations' table — out of scope per ID `active` boolean filter; these stations are decommissioned. Count verified post-cycle-2 audit (cycle-0/1 had stale '~50+').

Master visible-text renders Concordia's Country cell as 'Italy
France' (raw wikitext '{{Flagu|Italy}}
{{Flagu|France}}'), which is a 2-line stacked rendering inside a single cell — NOT a verbatim single-value string. Cycle-0 staged 'Italy/France' (slash-delimited) was non-verbatim AND non-standard. normalization_decisions.rule: Wikipedia master link-target labels stripped; visible-text station name only; footnote markers removed.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master station names link to per-station Wikipedia articles via wikilink markup; staged value uses the visible text only (e.g., 'Amundsen–Scott South Pole' NOT '[[Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station|Amundsen–Scott South Pole]]'). Unicode characters in station names preserved (en-dash in 'Amundsen–Scott'; apostrophe in 'Dumont d'Urville' and 'O'Higgins'; accented characters in 'San Martín' and 'Adélie Land' in Location).

normalization_decisions.rule: Master visible-text preserved verbatim including comma-separated compound locations and en-dashes.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Compound locations like 'Dome C, Antarctic Plateau' (Concordia), 'Laurie Island, South Orkney Islands' (Orcadas), 'Vesleskarvet, Queen Maud Land' (SANAE IV), 'Larsemann Hills, Prydz Bay' (Zhongshan), 'Inexpressible Island, Terra Nova Bay' (Qinling) preserved with internal commas. CSV cells with internal commas are properly double-quoted per RFC 4180.

normalization_decisions.rule: Master 'Year est.' integer preserved verbatim — does NOT always reflect original founding for stations with rebuilt/relocated/transferred history.
normalization_decisions.rationale: Master's 'Year est.' reflects current-facility-commissioning year for several rows (Halley 2013 = Halley VI; SANAE IV 1997 = current SANAE IV after I-III predecessors; Vernadsky 1994 = Ukrainian re-establishment after UK Faraday transfer 1996). Original-founding-year would diverge for these rows (Halley original 1956; Vernadsky as Faraday 1947). Staged value follows master to preserve source_defined claim. Per-row notes in universe_listing flag the rebuild/transfer nuances.

normalization_decisions.rule: In-scope universe = exactly the master's 'Permanent active stations' table rows (43 rows) — independent of whether individual rows are on the Antarctic continent or on Antarctic islands.
normalization_decisions.rationale: The master article uses a 4-partition structure (Permanent active stations table / Subantarctic stations subsection / Summer-only active stations table / Inactive stations table). The Subantarctic subsection is the master's explicit boundary marker for 'NOT Antarctic'. The in-scope Permanent active stations table includes Antarctic island stations (King George Island, Laurie Island, Anvers Island, Adelaide Island, Ross Island, Marambio Island, etc.) which the master groups under 'Antarctic'. Cycle-2 audit BLOCKING fix: earlier prose described the in-scope partition as 'continental-only', which contradicted the master's row content (>50% of in-scope rows are on Antarctic islands). Corrected predicate = source_partition='Permanent active stations table'.

open_questions.question: Should Concordia Country be staged as 'Italy; France' (current cycle-2 normalization) or as a two-row decomposition (one Italy row + one France row, with Concordia appearing twice)?
open_questions.resolution: Single row with multi-value Country cell 'Italy; France' preserves master's single-row structure (master shows Concordia as ONE row with a 2-value Country cell). Two-row decomposition would duplicate Station Name PK and lose the master's single-station truth. Resolution: keep single row with semicolon-delimited multi-value.

open_questions.question: Should Year Established preserve master's 'Year est.' even when it diverges from original founding year (Halley, Vernadsky, SANAE IV)?
open_questions.resolution: Yes — preserve master verbatim per source_defined claim. Per-row notes in universe_listing document the rebuild/transfer history. Alternative (using original-founding-year) would invalidate source_defined and require per-station Wikipedia article look-ups, inflating source_count beyond 1.

open_questions.question: Should Eduardo Frei and Villa Las Estrellas be decomposed into two rows (one research station + one civilian settlement)?
open_questions.resolution: No — master shows this as a single compound row. Decomposing would over-specify beyond master granularity. Civilian-settlement vs research-station distinction is not in master's data shape.

open_questions.question: Is `Science/Polar Research` the right domain, or should it be `Geography/Polar Regions`?
open_questions.resolution: Cycle-1 audit confirmed `Science/Polar Research` is acceptable per domain_taxonomy.md (answer entities are research facilities → Science framing). `Geography/Polar Regions` would also be defensible (spatial-membership emphasis) but is not required.

open_questions.question: Will future station commissionings (next decade) require row additions?
open_questions.resolution: temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this. The universe grows by ~1-2 stations per decade on historical average (Qinling 2024 is the most recent). New commissionings will require row additions to maintain source_defined claim against the live master article. Decommissioning is rare for permanent stations on benchmark timescales but possible.

open_questions.question: Does the master's 'Year est.' column genuinely show only the integer year, or does it sometimes encode month/day for very recent stations (e.g., Qinling 2024-02-07)?
open_questions.resolution: Master's Year est. column is integer-only across all 43 rows. Day-level precision (Qinling's 2024-02-07 opening) is mentioned in body text of Qinling's wiki article, NOT in the master table. Staged schema column_type=numeric is honest.

decision_log.decision: Universe = 43 permanent-active research stations (NOT 52 if Subantarctic included; NOT 88+ if Summer-only included)
decision_log.rationale: Master article has 4 partitions: Permanent active stations table (43, in scope), Subantarctic stations subsection (9, out of scope per master's own partition boundary which separates Antarctic from Subantarctic), Summer-only active stations (45, out of scope per 'year_round' ID), Inactive stations (69, out of scope per 'active' ID). The 43-row Permanent active partition is the canonical answer to the staged query. Cycle-2 audit corrected partition counts from cycle-0's stale '~57' (summer-only) and '~50+' (inactive) to live-source values 45 and 69.

decision_log.decision: Scope predicate = source_partition='Permanent active stations table' (NOT location_scope='continental_antarctica')
decision_log.rationale: CYCLE-2 BLOCKING FIX. Cycle-0/1 incorrectly described the in-scope partition as 'continental Antarctica only'. The master's 'Permanent active stations' table contains >50% Antarctic-island stations (King George Island, Laurie Island, Anvers Island, Adelaide Island, Ross Island, Marambio Island, Galindez Island, etc.). The correct master-aligned boundary is the partition structure itself: in-scope = the 'Permanent active stations' table partition (which the master treats as Antarctic, whether continental or island); out-of-scope = the master's separate 'Subantarctic stations' subsection (which the master treats as NOT Antarctic). Cycle-2 fix updated table_title, db_analog, temporal_note, claim_type_rationale, collection_summary, decision_log, and audit_trail to consistently use partition-based scope language.

Single-table boolean conjunction filter (status='active' AND operating_schedule='year-round' AND source_partition='Permanent active stations table') over master's 4-partition union. No multi-table join; no aggregation; no projection beyond column selection. operation_type vocab confirms 'filter' for boolean-conjunction-over-master-partitions shape.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (Station Name PK + Country + Location + Year Established)
decision_log.rationale: Master's 'Permanent active stations' table has 10 columns (Name, Location, Country, Administration, Year est., Max. pers., Summer pop., Winter pop., UTC offset, Mean annual temp.). Staged schema selects the 4 most-stable identification + temporal columns. Excluded: Administration (operator-organization details — would duplicate Country in many cases); Max. pers./Summer pop./Winter pop. (population values that fluctuate seasonally and across years); UTC offset (administrative timezone, not station-essential); Mean annual temp. (variable across years, less universal). The 4-col selection prioritizes stable identification + provenance attributes.

Master's 'Permanent active stations' table uses Station Name as the implicit row identifier. All 43 names are unique in the table. Single-key PK avoids composite-PK complexity since (Station Name, Country) and (Station Name, Year) would be over-specified — Station Name alone is unique.

decision_log.rationale: Master displays this as a single row even though Eduardo Frei is the research station and Villa Las Estrellas is the adjacent Chilean civilian settlement. Single-row preservation honors master structure; splitting would over-specify beyond master granularity.

decision_log.rationale: For some stations the master's 'Year est.' reflects current-facility-commissioning year (Halley 2013 = Halley VI commissioning; SANAE IV 1997 = current SANAE IV commissioning; Vernadsky 1994 = Ukrainian re-establishment after UK Faraday transfer) rather than original-station-founding year. Master's value preserved verbatim per source-defined claim; per-row notes in universe_listing flag these nuances. open_questions documents the resolution.

decision_log.decision: domain = Science/Polar Research (NEW subdomain under Science family)
decision_log.rationale: Antarctic research stations are scientific research facilities; Science family per domain_taxonomy.md is the closest fit (joining Science/Astronomy + Science/Volcanology + Science/Biology precedents). 'Polar Research' subdomain captures the polar-region specialization. Alternative 'Geography/Polar Regions' less ideal because the row universe is research facilities (Science framing) not geographic regions per se. Cycle-1 audit confirmed this choice is acceptable.

decision_log.decision: Entity class = engineered-structures/antarctic-research-stations (NEW fine-class within engineered-structures bucket)
decision_log.rationale: Research stations are built facilities, fitting the engineered-structures bucket (joining bridges, dams, tunnels, skyscrapers, canals fine-classes). 'antarctic-research-stations' specificity distinguishes from generic facilities; floor-lift adds 1 new fine-class to engineered-structures bucket.

New permanent stations are commissioned periodically (Qinling 2024, Jang Bogo 2014, Halley VI 2013, Bharati 2012, Concordia 2005, Neumayer III 2009, SANAE IV 1997, Vernadsky 1994). The universe count grows by ~1-2 stations per decade on average. Country distribution shifts as emerging powers (India, China, South Korea) commission stations. Decommissioning is rare for active permanent stations on benchmark timescales.
Master's 'Permanent active stations' table is alphabetically ordered by station name. Preserving master's sort order honors source-defined claim and simplifies row-level audit verification.
